LESSON: PARTS OF A PLANT • FLOWER • LEAF

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1
Subject: General
Strand: My Neighbourhood
Topic 4.3: Parts of a plant • Flower • Leaf
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Parts of a plant • Flower • Leaf, part of My Neighbourhood in SNE  /  visual-impairment / PP1 General.

Key inquiry question: Why do we have plants?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Parts of a plant • Flower • Leaf together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: learner develops exploration when manipulating parts of a plant.

Digital literacy : learner gains digital literacy skills as they watch and listen to audio visual clips on parts of a plant from digital devices.

Values:
• Love: learner enhances sharing when using pasting materials.

• Responsibility: learner enhances accountability when displaying mounted pictures of flowers on the wall

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Environmental education: learner enhances environmental awareness as they identify parts of plants.

Link to other learning area:

Plants can be used as a concrete object during counting in Mathematical Activities

Suggested Learning Resources

Charts, picture cards of flowers, flash cards, drawn pictures of flowers and leaves, embossed flowers and leaves, glue, crayons, realia, photos,

coloured pencils, slates, flowers, school environment, digital devices with assistive technology.
